summary: Registers the MIME types application/ISUP and application/QSIG so that telephone signaling messages can be carried inside SIP messages such as INVITE or INFO. This is useful when a SIP call is connected to the traditional telephone network. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Phone companies use their own secret-code messages. This gives those messages a label so they can ride inside internet phone calls without getting lost.

questions: how to carry isup in sip
what is the handling parameter in content-disposition
subtitle: Two MIME types that let SIP messages carry telephone-network signaling untouched.

tldr.problem: When a SIP call connects to the traditional phone network, ISUP or QSIG signaling data sometimes has to travel inside SIP messages, and it needs to be preserved exactly for phone features to work.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3204 registers the media types application/ISUP and application/QSIG for binary payloads, with a version parameter, an optional base parameter for ISUP, and a new signal disposition with a handling parameter.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard, updated by RFC 3459 and RFC 5621, and it is meant only for signaling used inside a SIP session, not as general transport.

today: RFC 3204 is a Proposed Standard from December 2001 and is updated by RFC 3459 and RFC 5621. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why SIP Needs ISUP and QSIG Types
sections.content:
ISUP (ISDN User Part, ITU-T Q.761-4) is a signaling protocol used between telephony switches. QSIG is the analogous protocol between private branch exchanges. In some set-ups, ISUP or QSIG information has to be carried between SIP entities as part of the payload of SIP messages, because the data must be preserved for the phone network's features to work properly.

The RFC limits its own scope. The types are for signaling used within the context of a SIP session, not general purpose transport of switched circuit network signaling. How the two sides agree that they are compatible is not covered and is assumed to be handled by other means, such as configuring the interworking functions. The document also says that using QSIG within SIP is neither endorsed nor recommended just because the MIME type is registered.
sections.eli5: When an internet call is joined to an old phone line, the phone line's special messages need a way to come along. This RFC gives them a ride, but only inside the call itself.

sections.title: The Two Media Types
sections.content:
ISUP and QSIG messages are arbitrary binary data that SIP does not interpret. The RFC chooses plain binary encoding over Base64, since Base64 would only add bulk and probably cost more processing. It points out that the MIME binary restrictions of RFC 2045 apply to Internet mail, not to SIP.

application/ISUP has a required version parameter and an optional base parameter. The ISUP message is encapsulated starting at the Message Type Code, leaving out the Routing Label and Circuit ID Code. application/QSIG has no required parameters and an optional version. Both are binary and refer to section 5 for security.
sections.eli5: The message is just a pile of bytes, so it is sent as is, like handing over a sealed package instead of copying it out by hand.

sections.title: Version and Base Parameters
sections.content:
The version parameter lets network administrators identify the ISUP version exchanged on a bilateral basis, so a SoftSwitch or Media Gateway Controller can parse the message correctly or reject it if the version is unsupported. The RFC puts no constraints on the values. Examples are a network-specific string such as X-NetxProprietaryISUPv3 or a standard one such as itu-t or ansi.

A base parameter can be added, for example when the receiver may not recognize the version string, to say that the content can also be processed using a named base specification. Nine base values are listed, along with whether the forward compatibility mechanism of ITU-T 1992 ISUP is supported.

For QSIG, version separates variants. The one listed value is iso, meaning ISO/IEC 11572 (Basic Call) and ISO/IEC 11582 (Generic Functional Protocol).
sections.eli5: The version is a sticker saying which dialect the message is written in. The base is a backup sticker saying a similar dialect will also do.

sections.title: Content-Disposition and the handling Parameter
sections.content:
A Content-Disposition header may be included to say how the encapsulated body should be processed. The default disposition-type for ISUP and QSIG bodies is signal, which means the body carries signaling information associated with the session but does not describe the session. The IANA section registers signal as a new disposition-type.

The new handling parameter tells the user agent server what to do with a body whose content type or disposition it does not understand. With optional the UAS MUST ignore the body. With required it MUST return 415 (Unsupported Media Type). If the parameter is missing, required is assumed.
sections.eli5: It is a note on the package saying what to do if you cannot read it: either shrug and carry on, or send it back and say you cannot take it.

sections.title: Examples in SIP INVITE Messages
sections.content:
Both examples are SIP INVITE requests with a multipart body. One part is SDP describing the session, and the other is the signaling object. The two parts are separated by a MIME boundary (unique-boundary-1 in the examples), which belongs to MIME multipart and is unrelated to the new types.

The ISUP example carries an ISUP IAM message with version=nxv3; base=etsi121. The QSIG example carries a QSIG SETUP message with version=iso. Because the payload is binary, each byte is sent as one byte, and the hex digits printed in the RFC are only for readability.
sections.eli5: An internet phone call carries two envelopes in one: one says how to talk, the other holds the phone company's coded message.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: ISUP and QSIG bodies may contain sensitive customer information, so encryption may be needed. The RFC points to the security mechanisms in RFC 2543 (SIP), which should be used as appropriate for both the SIP message and the encapsulated ISUP or QSIG body.
sections.eli5: The coded message may hold private details about callers, so it should be locked up the same way the rest of the call is.

sections.title: IANA Registration Rules
sections.content:
The document registers application/ISUP and application/QSIG. New version symbols must cite a definitive specification reference that names a particular issue, and the authors recommend a subject matter expert under the Expert Review policy of RFC 2434. If a specification is fully peer-to-peer backwards compatible with an earlier issue, no separate symbol is needed.

Symbols beginning with X- are reserved for non-standard use and may cross administrative domains only under a bilateral agreement. They fall under the Private Use policy of RFC 2434.
sections.eli5: New version stickers need a real rulebook behind them. Stickers starting with X- are private nicknames that only two agreeing companies use.

data.title: ISUP body part headers
data.code:
Content-Type: application/ISUP; version=nxv3; base=etsi121
Content-Disposition: signal; handling=optional
